sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: front seat versus all-passenger belt rules, restraint tiers, reaction versus braking distance, signal timing, slow-driving exceptions, carbon monoxide, tires and traffic stop extras
Confusable pairs among the everyday safe driving rules, plus continuation facts that complete part C; each block ties to one guide page, the stopping distance chart is a picture and is not described, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
The general belt law covers the driver and front seat riders, but with an intermediate license holder at the wheel the duty extends to every passenger. [A01]
Why it matters: group seat belts; confusable front seat versus all passengers; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
The two youngest restraint tiers work independently: under four years needs a child restraint at any weight, and under 40 pounds needs one at any age. [A01]
Why it matters: group child restraints; confusable age-only versus weight-only tiers; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A02
The booster tier needs all three conditions at once, while the safety belt tier is reached by meeting any one of eight years, 80 pounds or more than 4 feet 9 inches. [A02]
Why it matters: group child restraints; confusable and versus or thresholds; difficulty high.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A01
The child restraint law covers transport in any motor vehicle other than a school bus or a public carrier for hire. [A01]
Why it matters: group child restraints; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A04
Reaction distance is covered before you touch the brake, while braking distance is covered after; together they make stopping distance. [A04]
Why it matters: group stopping distance; confusable reaction versus braking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A04
The signaling rule of at least 100 feet has an exception: hold the signal until you pass any streets, driveways or entrances before your turn, or a vehicle about to enter between you and the turn. [A04]
Why it matters: group signals; confusable signal early versus wait; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A05
Going below a posted minimum is excused only by bad weather, heavy traffic or a bad road, while blocking traffic by slow driving is illegal even with no minimum posted. [A05]
Why it matters: group slow driving; confusable posted minimum versus no minimum; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A02
Good posture means sitting straight and relaxed against the seat, close enough to reach the pedals but with elbows still in front of you, both feet near the controls and both hands on the wheel. [A02]
Why it matters: group posture; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A02
The seven-to-nine and three-to-five hand positions are comfortable and let you make most turns without letting go of the wheel. [A02]
Why it matters: group steering; continuation of the grip rule.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A02
Look well down the road, not just right in front of the hood, to spot places you will need to steer or slow before you reach them. [A02]
Why it matters: group steering; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0058]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A03
If traffic is behind you when you want to parallel park, signal, pull up beside the space and wait for the traffic to pass before you back in. [A03]
Why it matters: group space behind; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A03
Pick a safe spot out of traffic to pick up or drop off passengers. [A03]
Why it matters: group space behind; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A03
If you are slowing others down, pull aside when safe to let them pass, using turnouts on some two-lane roads; other two-lane roads may offer passing lanes. [A03]
Why it matters: group space behind; confusable with the slow-poke law.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A03
Keep a wider gap from parked cars, because someone may step out of or between them, or one may pull out. [A03]
Why it matters: group space to the side; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A03
When traffic is merging onto a multi-lane road and the lane beside you is empty, move over a lane to make room. [A03]
Why it matters: group space to the side; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0059]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A04
Other drivers expect you to keep doing what you are doing, so warn them before you change direction or slow down to give them time to react. [A04]
Why it matters: group communication; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0060]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A05
A turn signal may not cancel itself after a small turn, so switch it off by hand if it has not clicked off. [A05]
Why it matters: group signals; continuation of signal shutoff.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A05
The horn is never for showing anger or frustration. [A05]
Why it matters: group horn; confusable warning use versus anger.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A05
Carbon monoxide from the engine is a deadly gas, so close the vents when following closely behind another vehicle and never drive with a broken muffler or exhaust. [A05]
Why it matters: group carbon monoxide; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A05
Take extra care where deer crossing signs are posted, and keep everyone belted and children in car seats to reduce injury if a deer crash happens. [A05]
Why it matters: group deer; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0061]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A06
Before slowing hard for a deer, make sure no one is behind you; heavy braking can dip the front end so the deer's body comes through into the passenger area. [A06]
Why it matters: group deer; confusable swerve versus brake; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A06
Read the right tire pressure in the owner's manual or on the driver's door jamb, check it with a gauge, and add or release air until it matches. [A06]
Why it matters: group tires; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A06
Check tires for wear and damage once a month or before a long trip. [A06]
Why it matters: group tires; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A06
Ask passengers at a traffic stop to stay calm, remain in the vehicle and keep their hands where the officer can see them. [A06]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; continuation of stop conduct.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A07
At night an officer may shine a spotlight on your car, so turn on the interior lights once you stop to help the officer see inside. [A07]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A07
Tell the officer where your documents are before reaching for them if they are out of reach, and expect an officer out of uniform to show credentials, which you may also request. [A07]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; continuation moved from part C.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A07
If asked to step out of the vehicle, stay well away from traffic and keep your hands visible. [A07]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A07
If you think an officer acted improperly, record what happened and report it promptly to that officer's agency, whose name and the officer's name appear on the ticket or can be requested. [A07]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec10-R29 | anchor: A07
During a traffic stop you keep constitutional rights, including freedom from unreasonable search and seizure, the right to remain silent and the right to an attorney. [A07]
Why it matters: group traffic stops; legal rights; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0063]
